subject: SIG: user provisioning & access evidence for procurement review
messages:
From: John Sullivan <j.sullivan@banyanhealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@banyanhealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: access provisioning and evidence request

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for sending the initial SIG stub. Our procurement/security team is kicking off a quick review focused on access controls (SSO, SCIM, RBAC, MFA, least privilege). To keep the process moving we need a couple of clarifications and artifacts by next Monday (2027-05-17):

- Can you confirm whether Redwood enforces SSO for all employee interactive logins (SAML 2.0)? Are contractor/guest accounts treated differently?
- SCIM: does push deprovisioning remove accounts immediately? What is the typical time window before tokens/API sessions are revoked? Please include any sample delta/export that shows a recent deprovisioning event.
- RBAC: we need a role matrix that maps SCIM groups to Redwood roles and the minimum permissions associated with each role.
- MFA: is MFA enforced for all interactive logins? Are there documented exceptions (service accounts, automation)? If so, what compensating controls exist?

Attachments that would help: SAML metadata, a SCIM sync delta CSV, RBAC role mapping CSV, and a snippet of the MFA policy.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the artifacts.

Regards,
John Sullivan
IT Security
Banyan Health

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: John Sullivan <j.sullivan@banyanhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, procure@banyanhealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:03:21 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: access provisioning and evidence request

John — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, and I attached the artifacts below. Let me know if you need anything deeper.

Summary answers:
- SSO/SAML: Redwood requires SAML 2.0 SSO for all interactive user logins by default. Contractors/guests can be placed in scoped groups with reduced permissions; we do not create separate auth pathways. SAML metadata attached (sso-saml-metadata.xml).
- SCIM provisioning: we support SCIM 2.0 push provisioning. Deprovisioning events (DELETE) are processed immediately; the associated account is marked disabled within the same request window and a background job revokes active interactive sessions and short-lived tokens within ~2–5 minutes (see sample log). SCIM sync delta attached (scim-sync-delta-20270510.csv).
- RBAC mapping: role names in our console are: admin, eng, manager, viewer, billing. Group->role mappings are configurable; attached is the exported mapping we use in the account demo (rbac-role-matrix-20270510.csv). The CSV includes minimal privilege columns (create/deploy/invoke/read).
- MFA: MFA is enforced for all interactive logins for staff by default. Service accounts and API keys are exempt from interactive MFA; those are restricted to scoped API tokens with rotation policies and IP allowlists where required. See snippet attached (mfa-policy-snippet.txt).

Attachments included: sso-saml-metadata.xml, scim-sync-delta-20270510.csv, rbac-role-matrix-20270510.csv, mfa-policy-snippet.txt.

Next steps: If the procurement team needs a short demo of deprovisioning behavior, I can run a live SCIM delete test and stream the audit/logs. Laura (cc'd) will coordinate any required slide deck for procurement.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: John Sullivan <j.sullivan@banyanhealth.com>

Sergio — thanks for the fast reply and the artifacts. Two quick clarifying items before we mark this closed: 

1) Deprovisioning timing: when you say tokens revoked in ~2–5 minutes, does that include long-lived API tokens issued to integrations? We need assurance that orphaned accounts cannot retain access.
2) SCIM deprovisioning failures: what retry/backoff behavior and auditing exists if the SCIM endpoint returns a 5xx?

If you can point me to a small log sample that shows a delete event and subsequent token revocation record, that will satisfy our evidence requirement.

Thanks,
John

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: John Sullivan <j.sullivan@banyanhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:47:03 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: access provisioning and evidence request

John — good questions. Pasting the relevant bits below and attaching a brief log snapshot (scim-deprovision-log-sample.txt).

- Long-lived API tokens: long-lived tokens are scoped and tied to service accounts (not user accounts). When a user account is deprovisioned via SCIM DELETE, any tokens issued to that user are flagged and included in the token-revocation job; those tokens are revoked by the same background process. Token revocation for user-bound tokens occurs within the 2–5 minute window; service-account tokens remain under the service-account rotation policy and must be explicitly revoked (we recommend using scoped automation, which we can help configure).

- SCIM error handling: our SCIM connector implements an exponential backoff on 5xx responses and will retry up to 5 times within a 15 minute window. Each failed attempt is logged with the request ID and timestamp; if the connector cannot deliver the change after retries it writes a high-severity incident to the audit stream and pings the account admins.

Sample log excerpt (from scim-deprovision-log-sample.txt):

2027-05-10T14:02:11Z | SCIM_DELETE | userId=ext-12345 | status=202 | queued-revoke-job=job-98765
2027-05-10T14:02:13Z | TOKEN_REVOKE | tokenId=tok-44b7 | subject=ext-12345 | result=revoked
2027-05-10T14:02:15Z | AUDIT_ENTRY | event=account.disabled | actor=scim-sync | id=evt-555

We can also provide a redacted event stream if you need the full sequence for compliance.

If that covers everything we can mark the SIG access section as complete and Laura can attach the artifacts to your procurement record. If you want the live demo I'll schedule it for later this week.

Regards,
Sergio
